14	// status_render.go owns the TEXT rendering of `entire-brain status`. Nothing
15	// here changes what the command computes, and in particular nothing here is
16	// reachable from --json: the machine contract is byte-identical to what it was
17	// before this file existed, and the JSON golden test enforces that.
18	//
19	// The problem it solves is that the default text report had become unreadable.
20	// On a real repository it printed forty-four "partial failure: E_MINIFIED …"
21	// lines, then the SAME forty-four files again as "blind spots", then a
22	// twenty-three-entry relation-type histogram — roughly 130 lines, of which
23	// about six carried information a person had asked for. The signal (is the
24	// backfill progressing? is the watcher alive? did a component fail?) was
25	// somewhere in the middle.
26	//
27	// So there are now two reports:
28	//
29	//   - DEFAULT: identity, the onboarding block, and a one-line health verdict.
30	//   - --verbose: everything the old report printed, except that repeated
31	//     warnings are collapsed to one line per group and no file is ever listed
32	//     twice across two sections.
33	//
34	// The grouping is not cosmetic. A repository that vendors JSON corpora is not
35	// forty-four separate problems; it is one fact ("data files are not source, and
36	// were not parsed as source") that the reader should be able to dismiss in one
37	// glance and go looking at in `doctor` if they care.
38	
39	// statusDataFileExtensions are the file types whose "not parsed as source"
40	// warning is expected rather than actionable: a JSON corpus, a lockfile, a
41	// sourcemap and a minified bundle are all DATA, and reporting each one as an
42	// individual semantic blind spot is noise with a 44:1 ratio.
43	var statusDataFileExtensions = map[string]bool{
44		".json": true, ".jsonl": true, ".ndjson": true, ".csv": true, ".tsv": true,
45		".map": true, ".lock": true, ".snap": true, ".svg": true, ".min.js": true,
46		".pb": true, ".bin": true, ".parquet": true,
47	}

49	// statusBlindSpotGroup is one collapsed reason plus the files it covers.
50	type statusBlindSpotGroup struct {
51		Code string
52		// Reason is the shared explanation, taken from the first member.
53		Reason string
54		Paths  []string
55		// DataFiles reports whether every member looks like a data file rather than
56		// unparsed source, which is what licenses the short "data files skipped"
57		// phrasing instead of a warning the reader should act on.
58		DataFiles bool
59	}

61	// Count reports how many files the group covers.
62	func (g statusBlindSpotGroup) Count() int { return len(g.Paths) }
63	
64	// Summary is the single line a collapsed group prints.
65	func (g statusBlindSpotGroup) Summary() string {
66		noun := "files"
67		if g.DataFiles {
68			noun = "data files"
69		}
70		if g.Count() == 1 {
71			noun = strings.TrimSuffix(noun, "s")
72		}
73		reason := strings.TrimSpace(g.Reason)
74		if reason == "" {
75			reason = strings.TrimSpace(g.Code)
76		}
77		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s skipped (%s)", g.Count(), noun, reason)
78	}

82		lowered := strings.ToLower(path)
83		if strings.HasSuffix(lowered, ".min.js") || strings.HasSuffix(lowered, ".min.css") {
84			return true

entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

input.title: Adopt enrich-at-source convention for brief's generic "X unavailable: <err>" warnings
input.description:
The brief and live-state warning arrays contain ~17 sites in `internal/cli/agent_surface.go` that wrap an arbitrary error as `"<thing> unavailable: " + err.Error()` (blind spots, semantic context, runtime trace, test suggestions, global memories, memories, freshness, HEAD/branch/diff probes, …). None states what stops working or what command fixes it. A wrap-site remedy would guess: the wrap cannot know why the underlying read failed.

PR https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/458 established the honest pattern for history artifacts: classify the failure at its source with a sentinel (`errFileHardlinked`) and attach the remedy there, so every surface that wraps it inherits the full sentence.

Work:
- Adopt this as the convention: degraded-state errors carry their own remedy at the point where the cause is known.
- Seed it with the highest-traffic wraps where the remedy is knowable: `memories unavailable` / `global memories unavailable` (store integrity → refresh + re-distill) and `semantic context unavailable` (provider/doctor errors already carry remedies after #458's follow-up).
- Leave wraps whose causes are genuinely heterogeneous as-is.

Inventory of all sites and their current texts: PR #458 description, "Flagged" section.

input.title: Fact review queue (proposals.json) has no recovery path when unreadable
input.description:
When `proposals.json` cannot be read, every surface shows `fact review queue unreadable; verify fact consistency before relying on these facts` (`retrieval_guard.go`, `facts_read_cmd.go`, brief warnings; unified-path caveat code `proposal_state_unavailable`). The message names no command because none exists — and unlike the history projection, this is not text-fixable: proposals are user data (pending reviews), not a derived projection, so no rebuild can recover them.

Design decision needed: should there be an explicit escape hatch, e.g. quarantine the unreadable file and start an empty queue behind an explicit acknowledge-loss flag (`memories review --reset-queue` or similar)? Until that exists, the degraded state is permanent and the message can only state the effect.

Context: flagged in the v0.2.0 degraded-state message audit, PR https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/458 ("Flagged" section, item 4).

input.title: Bench tooling must not hardlink-clone live brain state (use clonefile or a real copy)
input.description:
Found in the wild on a dev machine: a bench run (staged under `/tmp/cor2214-bench/data6/`, likely the COR-2214 harness) copied the live brain's `history/` tree with hardlinks. A hardlink raises nlink on the LIVE file it copies, which trips entire-brain's nlink>1 alias guard — every history read is then refused and history context silently drops out of each brief, recall, and query on the real brain.

PR https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/458 makes that state repairable (`entire brain memory repair`) and makes the refusal name the fix, but the harness keeps re-creating the condition on every run.

Fix in the bench tooling: replace the hardlink clone with APFS clonefile (`cp -c` on macOS) or a plain copy. Clonefile gives the same cheap copy-on-write semantics without touching the source files' link counts.

Relation to COR-2214: this issue is about the harness's clone step, not the benchmark itself.

17	// memory_receipts.go is the projection receipt: the durable, content-free
18	// proof of which canonical sessions the last full consolidation represented,
19	// at which input digests. Jobs are operational history; a deterministic job
20	// is complete only when its identity appears here (or its session is
21	// tombstoned). The receipt is published through the Brain manifest, whose
22	// atomic replacement is the commit point.
23	
24	const (
25		projectionStateFileName = "projection-state-v1.json"
26		projectionStateRel      = historyDirName + "/" + projectionStateFileName
27		projectionSchemaVersion = 1
28		// projectionReconcilerVersion mirrors the overlay's reconciliation rule
29		// version: receipts from a different rule are stale.
30		projectionReconcilerVersion = historyShortTermReconcilerVersion
31	)
32	
33	type projectionReceipt struct {
34		SessionRef    string    `json:"session_ref"`
35		SessionID     string    `json:"session_id"`
36		Branch        string    `json:"branch,omitempty"`
37		InputDigest   string    `json:"input_digest"`
38		ExchangeCount int       `json:"exchange_count"`
39		CompletedAt   time.Time `json:"completed_at"`
40	}
41	
42	type projectionState struct {
43		SchemaVersion     int                 `json:"schema_version"`
44		ReconcilerVersion int                 `json:"reconciler_version"`
45		GeneratedAt       time.Time           `json:"generated_at"`
46		Sessions          []projectionReceipt `json:"sessions"`
47	}
48	
49	// projectionStateReadState keeps operationally distinct receipt failures
50	// separate. In particular, a newer schema must never be treated as corrupt
51	// disposable state: callers can report it and leave it untouched until this
52	// binary is upgraded.
53	type projectionStateReadState string
54	
55	const (
56		projectionStateAbsent      projectionStateReadState = "absent"
57		projectionStateCurrent     projectionStateReadState = "current"
58		projectionStateCorrupt     projectionStateReadState = "corrupt"
59		projectionStateStale       projectionStateReadState = "stale"
60		projectionStateUnsafe      projectionStateReadState = "unsafe"
61		projectionStateUnsupported projectionStateReadState = "unsupported"
62	)
63	
64	type projectionStateLoadError struct {
65		State   projectionStateReadState
66		Code    string
67		Path    string
68		Version int
69		Action  string
70		Detail  string
71	}
72	
73	func (e *projectionStateLoadError) Error() string {
74		if e == nil {
75			return ""
76		}
77		detail := strings.TrimSpace(e.Detail)
78		if detail == "" {
79			detail = string(e.State)
80		}
81		return fmt.Sprintf("%s: projection receipt %s: %s", e.Code, e.Path, detail)
82	}
83	
84	// projectionStateAction names the command that clears each state.
85	//
86	// `memory` is a subcommand of THIS binary, not a verb of the host CLI, so the
87	// repair command has to carry the brain's own spelling. It was printed as
88	// `entire memory repair` -- a command neither dispatch mode can resolve: a
89	// standalone reader has no `entire` at all, and a plugin reader's `entire`
90	// dispatches `memory` to nothing. The spelling comes from setupCommandPrefix,
91	// read from the process environment the same way path.go, workspace.go and
92	// agent_surface.go read it -- these printers sit too deep in the health/error
93	// path to be handed one.
94	func projectionStateAction(state projectionStateReadState) string {
95		brainCmd := setupCommandPrefix(os.LookupEnv)
96		switch state {
97		case projectionStateAbsent:
98			return "run `" + brainCmd + " memory repair` to rebuild the missing disposable receipt"
99		case projectionStateStale:
100			return "run `" + brainCmd + " memory repair` to atomically publish a receipt matching current canonical sessions"
101		case projectionStateUnsafe:
102			return "run `" + brainCmd + " memory repair` — the unsafe receipt is never read; a fresh generation is rebuilt from canonical sessions"
103		case projectionStateUnsupported:
104			return "this newer receipt is left untouched; upgrade entire-brain with `entire plugin upgrade brain` (local-dev installs: rebuild and reinstall)"
105		case projectionStateCorrupt:
106			return "inspect the reported receipt, then run `" + brainCmd + " memory repair` to rebuild disposable state"
107		default:
108			return ""
109		}
110	}
111	
112	func newProjectionStateLoadError(state projectionStateReadState, path, detail string, version int) error {
113		code := memoryErrStateCorrupt
114		switch state {
115		case projectionStateUnsupported:
116			code = memoryErrUnsupportedVersion
117		case projectionStateStale:
118			code = memoryErrSourceStale
119		case projectionStateUnsafe:
120			code = memoryErrStateUnsafe
121		}
122		return &projectionStateLoadError{
123			State: state, Code: code, Path: path, Version: version,
124			Action: projectionStateAction(state), Detail: detail,
125		}
126	}
127	
128	// sessionTranscriptDigest hashes the exported transcript file (streamed).
129	func sessionTranscriptDigest(brainDir, rel string) (string, error) {
130		data, err := readCanonicalHistoryTranscript(context.Background(), brainDir, rel)
131		if err != nil {
132			return "", err
133		}
134		sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
135		return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]), nil
136	}
137	
138	// buildProjectionReceipts derives the receipt set from the canonical manifest
139	// and the just-built index. A valid empty session succeeds with zero
140	// exchanges; tombstoned sessions are represented by the tombstone, never a
141	// receipt. An unreadable transcript simply has no receipt: reconciliation
142	// keeps its job open.
143	func buildProjectionReceipts(brainDir string, manifest *exportManifest, index historyIndex, now time.Time) (projectionState, error) {
144		stones, _, err := loadSessionTombstonesChecked(brainDir)
145		if err != nil {
146			return projectionState{}, err
147		}
148		return buildProjectionReceiptsFromSnapshot(brainDir, manifest, stones, index, now), nil
149	}
150	
151	func buildProjectionReceiptsFromSnapshot(brainDir string, manifest *exportManifest, stones sessionTombstones, index historyIndex, now time.Time) projectionState {
152		state := projectionState{SchemaVersion: projectionSchemaVersion, ReconcilerVersion: projectionReconcilerVersion, GeneratedAt: now}
153		if manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil || manifest.Sources.Sessions == nil {
154			return state
155		}
156		exchangesByPath := map[string]int{}
157		for _, record := range index.Records {
158			if record.Kind == conversationKind {
159				exchangesByPath[record.Path]++
160			}
161		}
162		seen := map[string]bool{}
163		for _, session := range manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions {
164			id := strings.TrimSpace(session.SessionID)
165			if id == "" {
166				continue // no canonical receipt identity; reconciliation keeps it open
167			}
168			if _, excluded := stones.Excluded[id]; excluded {
169				continue
170			}
171			rel := filepath.ToSlash(strings.TrimSpace(session.TranscriptPath))
172			if rel == "" {
173				continue
174			}
175			digest, err := sessionTranscriptDigest(brainDir, rel)
176			if err != nil {
177				continue // no receipt: the job for this session stays open
178			}
179			branch := strings.TrimSpace(session.Branch)
180			if branch == "" {
181				branch = strings.TrimSpace(manifest.Sources.Sessions.DefaultBranch)
182			}
183			ref, _ := conversationSessionRef(manifest.RepoKey, branch, id, digest)
184			if seen[ref] {
185				continue // re-export duplicates resolve to one receipt (newest-first manifest order not guaranteed; digest ties break by first)
186			}
187			seen[ref] = true
188			state.Sessions = append(state.Sessions, projectionReceipt{
189				SessionRef: ref, SessionID: id, Branch: branch,
190				InputDigest: digest, ExchangeCount: exchangesByPath[rel], CompletedAt: now,
191			})
192		}
193		sort.Slice(state.Sessions, func(i, j int) bool { return state.Sessions[i].SessionRef < state.Sessions[j].SessionRef })
194		return state
195	}

No JSON key or error-code prefix changed.
